sources.prompt:
Production asset sheet for a Don't Starve Together 2D cutout character build. NOT a concept board. Transparent background, no text, no grids, no shadows.
Image 1 is the ORIGINAL HEADBASE frame guide (four heads in one row). Image 2 is the ORIGINAL HAT-HEAD frame guide (four cropped heads). Image 3 is the approved NEW Wili art style and character identity.
Draw exactly EIGHT separate HEAD-ONLY sprites in a tidy FOUR-COLUMN by TWO-ROW grid. Leave generous fully transparent space between sprites.
TOP ROW: reproduce the four orientations/uses of Image 1 in the same order: 0 front head, 1 side profile facing RIGHT, 2 back of head, 3 stylized electrocution skull head.
BOTTOM ROW: the same four orientations as Image 2, with the TOP HAIR flattened/cropped for hats, like that guide.
Redesign the normal heads as the approved Wili: angular midnight-blue hair, a pale silver-white lock near the left/front fringe, chalk-ivory skin, black charcoal cloth half-mask over the lower face. Hair is sharp and asymmetrical but compact enough for the existing game rig. NO ponytails on these heads: ponytail is a separate sprite. NO neck, shoulders, body, hats or accessories outside the head.
CRITICAL: normal front/profile heads must have BLANK SKIN WHERE THE EYES AND BROWS WILL GO. Do NOT draw any eyes, eyebrows, eyelashes, pupils or nose on normal heads. The game overlays a separate face sprite. Keep the visible blank eye-window position and scale close to the original guides so the overlay fits. Do not put fringe across the middle of that eye window. Back view has no face or mask painted on the back.
Skull frames remain stylized ivory skulls with dark eye sockets, not normal human faces; echo the new hair silhouette in the black outline as needed.
Maintain each guide's pose and roughly the same width/height ratios. The bottom row must be shorter at the TOP for hats, not squashed faces. Same character design in every view. Bold scratchy black ink, flat navy/charcoal fills and sparse silver hatching, matching the approved game art. Genuine alpha transparency; no labels, numbers, checkerboard drawn into the image, border, backdrop or extra parts.

Production cutout sprite sheet for Wili, genuinely transparent, no text or grid.
Image 1 is the original ponytail frame guide; Image 2 is the original cheeks component guide; Image 3 is the approved new character.
Draw exactly FIVE separate components in a THREE-column TWO-row layout, with large transparent gaps:
Top row, left to right:
1. The visible ponytail from original frame 1 (second cell): hair attached by a small red tie at the upper-left, tail arcs down-right.
2. The visible ponytail from original frame 2 (third cell): attachment at the upper-right, tail arcs down-left.
3. The skeleton/electrocution ponytail from original frame 4 (last cell): preserve its black and ivory segmented special-state nature and same general outline.
Do NOT draw the original almost-empty frame 0 or empty frame 3: those are invisible placeholders.
New normal ponytails must match Wili's angular midnight-blue low ponytail with a muted red binding, split into a few sharp compact locks, sparse dark ink hatching. They are ONLY detached ponytails, not complete heads, bangs, ears or faces. Preserve the source orientations and attachment placement.
Bottom row: ONLY TWO cheek sprites from Image 2, one per left and middle cell. These are small rounded pale-ivory skin patches with restrained dark ink edge, same round/tilted shapes as the source; no eyes or facial marks. Last bottom-right cell is empty.
Keep the source part proportions and silhouette roles so these attach to the original game rig. No neck, body, hands, weapons, background, grid, labels, numbers, shadow or decorative lighting. This is an engineering component sheet, not a composed illustration.
